newsitem.title: HUNGARY: PM SAYS HUNGARY BOMBING WAVE CRACKED, PROBE GOES ON.
newsitem.headline: PM SAYS HUNGARY BOMBING WAVE CRACKED, PROBE GOES ON.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn said on Tuesday police had achieved a breakthrough in solving a Budapest bombing wave started last September in the biggest criminal investigation since he came to power in 1994.

"The investigation is still going on but billions of forints were misappropriated," Horn told a news conference. "This could prove to be the turning point in both the bombing wave and in uncovering serious fraud."
Last week, when announcing the arrests of 13 suspects, police said the bombings were devised to divert police attention from fuel tax and excise duty evasion amounting to "billions of forints".
Police said earlier that almost two dozen explosions of grenades and petrol bombs, most of which happened in Budapest since September, were linked to an escalating gang turf war.

Minister of Interior Gabor Kuncze, also present at the news conference, said the cases go back to the early 1990s when (subsidised) heating oil was sold as vehicle fuel with illegal incomes amounting to tens of billions of forints.
Horn said police officers and top customs officials were prosecuted in connection with the cases but added that "there is no indication that other state agencies are involved".
